chunk_map.heading: Change the rules on recurrence, not one miss

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: line 10 "After a bad night, the next one is usually better" - 'night' resolves to the nightly digest run named at line 4 ("one digest") and line 8; 'it' at line 4 binds to "One wrong line"; 'the note' line 8 binds to "worth a note" line 4. Harm (unresolvable referent on the wall) absent.
No pointer to another file or lecture by position; closest is line 14-style provenance, which sits in the maintainer block, outside the body. grep for 'opening|earlier lecture|that story' in body: 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: line 10 "After a bad night" is a generic scenario, not 'the X you did/saw/caught'; no beat-in-room reference in lines 1-10.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess/predict or demo beat on the slide

rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 8 "Wait for the same mistake to come back... That is when the note becomes a rule." is a self-carrying claim; slide holds four full declarative paragraphs (lines 4-10).
Header line 1 "Change the rules on recurrence, not one miss" matches body: line 4 one miss = a note, line 8 recurrence = rule. Nothing contradicts it.

Closest: line 4 "One wrong line in one digest is worth a note. It is not yet a reason to change the rules." - one negation, not a Not X. Not Y. Z. triple; no anaphora triple, no superlative, no number+retraction, no noun stack, no verb triplet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: line 6 'tampering' is Deming's term, bolded and glossed in-sentence ("reacting to every ordinary variation"), ordinary stats vocabulary not repo dialect; grep for surface/firing/compendium/beat/mood in body: 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget - bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: One bold element on the slide, line 6 "**tampering**" (1 word, a coined term/handle); within <=1 budget and <=5-word cap.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content - verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Included as a standalone slide-include line at curriculum/lectures/apt101-write-it-down-or-lose-it.md:7 "[Change the rules on recurrence, not one miss](slides/change-on-recurrence.md)", the transparent include path; renders in the composed deck.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering - position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/slides/change-on-recurrence.md -> 'OK - 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.' exit 0; no hand-numbered header.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/slides/change-on-recurrence.md -> 'OK - 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' exit 0; grep above/below/earlier/previous in body: 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no in-body links on the slide; rule is a review surface, not a gate

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size - 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/slides/change-on-recurrence.md -> 'oversized: 0', 'every slide is within limits' exit 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture slide header line 1 "Change the rules on recurrence, not one miss" states a prescriptive claim with its contrast clause, not a bare label; matches the lecture-heading-as-claim convention (cf. 'Gates decay').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies - three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: line 4 "It is not yet a reason to change the rules." partly echoes the header, but it carries the move (a miss is a note, not a rule change) and lines 6/8/10 each add a distinct object (Deming term, recurrence test, regression to the mean); no closing koan, no design commentary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: git log shows header '+## Change the rules on recurrence, not one miss' only as an add in the file's creation; no rename-without-body-change commit; body (lines 4-10) answers the header.
